messages:
Emma S: Hey team — escalation from AcmeCorp. They rotated keys in their KMS ~30m ago and immediately started getting 401s from our hosted API. Customer says requests that previously worked now fail with mixed 401/503. Tim from AcmeCorp pasted logs, says their rotation went through; they expect our system to pick up the new key.
Noah R: thanks Emma. any correlation id or sample request from Acme?
Emma S: pasted sample curl from Tim:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_acmecorp_newkey" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-x","input":"hi"}' -v
> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
> x-request-id: rq_1234abcd
> content-type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```
Olivia K: hmm, error = invalid_api_key not rate limited. He also reported intermittent 503s from our edge: `upstream service unavailable` in Traefik logs.
Emma S: customer: "We rotated via our KMS (Google KMS) and updated the secret backing our env in their infra. We also have webhook to push to ours but we didn't touch Redwood configs — we expected your system to accept the new key."
Noah R: quick theory — their key rotation created a new key id that our KMS-sync job didn't reconcile because of a long watch interval + transient Vault cache. Could cause some requests to hit old backend that still has cached key and return 401 while routing intermittently to old pool that returns 503.
Olivia K: can we get the server-side view for that x-request-id? I want to see which API key id our auth layer resolved for rq_1234abcd.
Deploy Bot: request-log: rq_1234abcd -> edge node eu-3 -> auth-service v2.7.1 -> key-hash: sha256:deadbeef -> lookup_time: 2026-03-15T14:02:12Z -> vault-cache-age: 00:05:23
Noah R: vault-cache-age of 5m — interesting. What is Acme's rotation TTL? If they set short TTL for old key, could be tokens being revoked at KMS level causing lookup failures in our auth-service when we try to validate older signatures.
Emma S: Tim says rotated at 13:30 UTC, and webhook delivered at 13:31; our logs show cache update at 13:36. So ~5m lag. Customer wants explanation + immediate mitigation.
Olivia K: reproduce locally: run our auth-service with a mocked Vault response that flips key material at t0 but returns old key until our `reconcile_interval` elapses. Code snippet: 
```go
// simplified reconcile loop
for range time.Tick(reconcileInterval) {
  keys := vault.ListKeys() // may return stale snapshot
  cache.Replace(keys)
}
```
Noah R: got it. Looks like reconcileInterval defaults to 5m in hosted. If their webhook is best-effort, this can cause up to 5m of drift. Plus we also have a kv-sidecar that caches secrets with its own refresh of 1m but edge auth goes directly to auth-service which reads the central cache.
Emma S: what's the immediate mitigation we can recommend to customer? They want to finish rotation now.
Olivia K: two options: 1) instruct customer to rotate in a way that keeps old key valid for a short overlap window (recommended), or 2) force-reload our cache for their tenant — we can trigger a manual reconcile for tenant acmecorp. I can run a tenant cache refresh if we allow it.
Noah R: I'm going to trigger a manual reconcile and watch the traces. Olivia, can you watch errors?
Deploy Bot: running manual_reconcile --tenant acmecorp --sync-now
Deploy Bot: manual_reconcile: started (cmd=manual_reconcile --tenant acmecorp --sync-now)
Deploy Bot: manual_reconcile: completed in 12.2s -> updated 1 key entries -> new cache-age 00:00:00
Vault Watcher Bot: vault change detected for acmecorp at 2026-03-15T14:36:12Z -> published event -> subscribers notified
Olivia K: after reconcile, edge trace for rq_1234abcd shows auth-service resolving new key id and request now returns 200 for a replayed request. Verified with synthetic: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_acmecorp_newkey" ...` returned 200.
Emma S: told Tim we did a manual reconcile and to retry now. He confirms success and apologizes for impact.
Noah R: root cause writeup in brief: reconcile_interval of auth-service set to 5m + webhook delivery timing caused up to 5m window where our cache had old key material. During rotation, some edge nodes forwarded to auth replicas that still had old cache leading to 401s; some requests hit unhealthy upstreams returning 503.
Olivia K: mitigation: 1) lower reconcile_interval to 30s for hosted auth-service (config flag) 2) add tenant-scoped push endpoint so customers can POST /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/reload-keys to force refresh from KMS/Vault when they rotate keys 3) add alert rule: spike in invalid_api_key errors after a rotation event -> notify oncall.
Noah R: I'll open a PR for config change + alert. Olivia, can you spec the reload endpoint? I'll add integration tests.
Olivia K: PR + test plan in progress. Test includes simulated KMS rotation and asserting no >15s window of 401s after webhook.
Emma S: action items for support: 1) notify Acme we completed manual refresh and to keep a short overlap window on rotations; 2) offer a checklist for rotation (steps + expected propagation times) 3) follow up once reload endpoint is live.
Emma S: thanks team. Posting the quick customer summary to the ticket now. :thumbsup:
